host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

Because this core exposes no standard system-memory region, the bounded oracle found one uniquely marked WRAM region in retro_serialize output and independently checked 58/58 two-player and 145/145 five-player port-two-multitap observations. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

Two-player and Four Score topologies both passed with individual-button and RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_MASK callback modes: 42/42 byte-exact observations per two-player run and 84/84 per Four Score run, 252/252 total. Every connected player was independently stimulated; published active-low NES register bytes matched exactly, and disconnected ports received zero queries. A separate exact-hash, fresh-process libretro probe used private save/state/system roots. An original 24,592-byte battery NROM (sha256 0ae807dfe80d7178f082e0d6297e94b145d2880ff5a974fa5c1b26f6bf1beaaa) executed and published LBSR01 from its 8,192-byte save RAM; a fresh process loaded that .srm (sha256 35f57192c251084b91b1a5fbfda019c4294db3266df377689c96a5769317745e), executed the cartridge, and published LBSR02, producing sha256 de5232a4b6205e474f7c169fda3dc0f1a22f3edd770c798340f7ee4571d2e124. Real Faxanadu content (sha256 9e5f12c5fb7f6aa2b360538038abc682488511293e79b9bd2ef199877a8c6d1d) produced a 13,772-byte state (sha256 d7c665ad5e6cf0d876edc2c5b8653edf883dc7313dcd1f334b3633fc1de5fffa): after deliberately replacing system-RAM bytes 0x100..0x107, same-process load restored LBSTATE1, and a fresh process started with 0effffffffffffff there before loading the same file and restoring LBSTATE1. host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

An original Z80 Game Gear controller diagnostic passed all 22/22 hardware-register observations in both individual-button and RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_MASK callback modes; the core exposed 8,192 bytes of work RAM, two complete controller-choice lists, and 96 descriptors. A separate permanent four-worker oracle used private roots and an original 65,536-byte mapper cartridge (sha256 132f435ad5f427bf20c16ab9dd06a68da1f62574ba9fb4ef500efb8eef700962): the executing program published LBSG01, then a fresh process loaded the six modified save bytes (sha256 e06cae62059ea3f685b6531f8db5eb0323807fc81b0b388b2c396c7a72493b3e) and published LBSG02, yielding sha256 2d18216b5ae17102aa2f4f61b02684b7ea10a388cb92d1c9c7e1ef51d82249dd. Its 1,036,288-byte state (sha256 f7d88c8408abf8263f0c2d68b51b3b1206850fe563a656f9be7f51260e1fd0eb) restored LBSTATE1 after deliberate mutation in the same and a fresh process. This proves this core binary's callback, save-memory, and serialization behavior, not RetroArch GUI/path handling, physical capture, firmware acceptance, or sync export/restore. Save sync remains blocked because no real provider export/restore was exercised.

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

test_notes: 2026-09-12: installed Mesen 0.9.9 core, mesen_libretro.so sha256 552f8ab6ac1fd08bd555f589eb999be73a469c79ccfa929f884adb2cf3366b43. An original generated NES NROM diagnostic exercised the real libretro core through the controller probe. Two-player and Four Score topologies both passed with individual-button and RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_MASK callback modes: 42/42 byte-exact observations per two-player run and 84/84 per Four Score run, 252/252 total. Every connected player was independently stimulated and published active-low NES register bytes matched exactly. In bitmask mode Mesen queried all five frontend ports even when ports were disconnected, but deliberately nonzero synthetic states on disconnected ports never reached NES hardware; per-port query counts are preserved by the probe report. A separate exact-hash, fresh-process libretro probe used private save/state/system roots. An original 24,592-byte battery NROM (sha256 0ae807dfe80d7178f082e0d6297e94b145d2880ff5a974fa5c1b26f6bf1beaaa) executed and published LBSR01 from its 8,192-byte save RAM; a fresh process loaded that .srm (sha256 35f57192c251084b91b1a5fbfda019c4294db3266df377689c96a5769317745e), executed the cartridge, and published LBSR02, producing sha256 de5232a4b6205e474f7c169fda3dc0f1a22f3edd770c798340f7ee4571d2e124. Real Faxanadu content (sha256 9e5f12c5fb7f6aa2b360538038abc682488511293e79b9bd2ef199877a8c6d1d) produced a 35,840-byte state (sha256 779f3ebb5a906fda3bd17cbcd7a6e1e61be0c5546dfc07cc529620d95c65495e): after deliberately replacing system-RAM bytes 0x100..0x107, same-process load restored LBSTATE1, and a fresh process started with 0e00000000000000 there before loading the same file and restoring LBSTATE1. This proves core-level persistent save-RAM reload and behavioral state restoration for these exact bytes, not RetroArch GUI/path handling, physical GUI capture, or sync export/restore. The save-sync status remains blocked because no real provider export/restore has been exercised on this host.

The original SNES hardware-register diagnostic passed all 58/58 two-player individual-button observations through the core's 131,072-byte WRAM region, including Start and Select despite their omission from its descriptor table. The core does not negotiate RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_MASK. Its advertised multitap path failed before button cases: the released-state readback was [0000,0000,0000,ffff,0000] rather than five released controllers, so controller status remains fail. A separate four-worker persistence oracle used the original SRAM LoROM: a fresh process consumed LBSG01 and published LBSG02 from an 8,192-byte save, and a 550,912-byte state restored LBSTATE1 after mutation in the same and a fresh process. This proves direct-core save memory and behavioral state restoration, not RetroArch frontend paths, optional firmware, physical capture, or sync. Save sync remains blocked because no real-provider export/restore was exercised.

Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

An original ARM GBA controller diagnostic passed all 26/26 KEYINPUT observations in both individual-button and RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_MASK callback modes; the core exposed 32,768 bytes of EWRAM and 16 input descriptors. A separate permanent four-worker oracle used private roots and an original 4,096-byte SRAM cartridge (sha256 272a6bd18723cb246342359c414e5515968152e2e31d54ffa4d27c96211c3030): the executing program published LBSG01, then a fresh process loaded the 32,768-byte save (sha256 d914ccf5f18d569cb1091616551130d2454655f2087588d7195a9da279f38d8f) and published LBSG02, yielding sha256 b53471673e7872e8de73c5a75a448d0d60bea5b27908fc0c53b29b1385df4d93. Its 430,144-byte state (sha256 b27f8f06b608f7b5d8f8132d682ef7f2f2e0b717a3601a24756064784a97bb90) restored LBSTATE1 after deliberate mutation in the same and a fresh process. This proves this core binary's callback, save-memory, and serialization behavior, not RetroArch GUI/path handling, physical capture, firmware acceptance, or sync export/restore. host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

host_notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

controller_config_path_and_syntax: Controller config is the [sdl] mapperfile setting pointing at a mapper file - by default mapper-sdl2-<version>.map stored alongside the primary config (i.e. ~/.config/dosbox/). Mapper files are plain text; each line maps an event name to one or more bindings: event_name "binding_1" "binding_2", e.g. key_esc "key 41" "stick_0 button 6"; keyboard bindings are key <scancode> with optional mod1/mod2/mod3 modifiers. Pre-configured per-game profiles ship in resources/mapperfiles and are loaded by name (mapperfile = xbox/doom.map). --erasemapper deletes only the default mapper file. [syntax/naming: mapper-sdl2-<version>.map by default; plain-text event_name "binding" lines, or a bundled resources/mapperfiles profile name] || ~/.config/dosbox/dosbox-staging.conf (primary config with global settings; other common XDG locations are also looked up on Linux; found via --printconf, edited via --editconf, recreated with defaults via --eraseconf). Additionally a local per-game config named dosbox.conf in the startup/working directory is loaded after the primary config; the [autoexec] section must be last. Portable mode: an empty dosbox-staging.conf beside the executable makes that folder the config root. Settings are plain text section/key=value, editable at runtime via CONFIG -set.

save_locations: Default common.save_path = RomFolder: the SRAM file sits next to the ROM. common.save_path in jgenesis-config.toml redirects: EmulatorFolder -> <directory containing the AppImage>/saves/<rom extension> (the AppImage path comes from the $APPIMAGE env var on AppImage builds); Custom -> <common.custom_save_path>/<rom extension>, and custom_save_path defaults to ~/.local/share/jgenesis/saves. The <rom extension> subdirectory mirrors the ROM's own extension (game.gen -> saves/gen, game.md -> saves/md, game.smc -> saves/smc)
save_naming: <ROM file name with its extension replaced by .sav> in the chosen location, e.g. Sonic.sfc -> Sonic.sav; multi-disc ' (Disc N)' suffixes are stripped; zip/7z inputs keep the archive's basename (game.zip -> game.sav). All cartridge cores persist SRAM through the SaveWriter "sav" extension; Sega CD backup RAM also lands in .sav and the 32X RAM cartridge uses .ramc
state_locations: Same three-way choice via common.state_path (default RomFolder: next to the ROM; EmulatorFolder -> <AppImage directory>/states/<rom extension>; Custom -> <common.custom_state_path>/<rom extension>, defaulting to ~/.local/share/jgenesis/states). common.load_recent_state_at_launch can autoload the most recent slot
state_naming: <ROM basename without extension>_<slot>.jst for slots 0-9 (SAVE_STATE_SLOTS=10), e.g. Sonic.sfc -> Sonic_0.jst .. Sonic_9.jst; contents are a 'jgenstate' header + version + zstd-compressed bincode; default hotkeys F5 save / F6 load the current slot, [ and ] step slots

Per-game saves are directory entries INSIDE this image (created/managed by the emulated Saturn BIOS); Kronos flushes writes to bupfilename on BackupFlush/BackupDeinit. save_locations: Single internal backup RAM image at Memory/Path, default getDataDirPath() + "/bkram.bin" - on non-Windows desktop builds getDataDirPath() is QStandardPaths::AppConfigLocation with the application name 'YabaSanshiro' (empty organization), i.e. ~/.config/YabaSanshiro, so the default image is ~/.config/YabaSanshiro/bkram.bin. save_naming: bkram.bin is one formatted backup memory volume, not per-game files: Yaba Sanshiro maps it with the 'BackUpRam Format' header check; with Memory/ExtendMemory (default true) it is an extended 8 MiB image (tweak_backup_file_size = 8*1024*1024, devmiyax extended-Backup RAM mapped at 0x06300000), otherwise a 64 KiB (0x10000) image; files over 10 MiB are reformatted, undersized files extended. Per-game saves are directory entries INSIDE this image (created/managed by the emulated Saturn BIOS), listed/copied/deleted through the in-app Backup Manager (BackupManager.cpp getFilelist/putFile/copy) rather than existing as separate files
state_locations: Directory from General/SaveStates, default getDataDirPath() = ~/.config/YabaSanshiro; autorun can load a slot at boot (autostart/load/slot)
state_naming: <disc product number>_<slot>.yss with the slot as 3 digits: YabSaveStateSlot/YabLoadStateSlot build "%s/%s_%03d.yss" from cdip->itemnum (the product number sscanf'd from offset 0x20 of the SEGA SEGASATURN disc header, e.g. GS-9122) and the slot number; the Save/Load State menus enumerate files matching <serial>_*.yss with a (\d+) slot capture; free-name dialogs use the filter 'Yabause Save State (*.yss)'
